fixture_repair.preimage_method: inverse-applied U6.21's edit textually: removed the _make_fixture_docket_verifiable definition block and its call from tests/test_dashboard.py, then compared sorted assert lines (283 == 283, identical) and the def test_ list (58 == 58, identical). LIMIT: a textual reconstruction, not a VCS blob (git HEAD is 48 tests behind the working tree), so it proves the edit is assertion-neutral, not that the reconstruction equals any committed revision.
fixture_repair.design_view: The repair is genuine (the artifact really does verify ok) but the normaliser belongs in build.py, as U6.21 itself handed up. Patching the fixture from the test side means: (1) anyone running build.py directly - the documented way to build the fixture tree - still gets an invalid ok-docket, so the fixture's name lies outside pytest; (2) a future reader diffing build.py sees no producer on a CONFIRMS claim and may 'fix' the verifier instead of the fixture; (3) the normaliser is invisible from the artifact side, so the invariant 'ok-docket verifies ok' is enforced by a test-side rewrite rather than by construction. Move producer='model' onto the C1 Claim in write_docket and delete the normaliser; keep one comment naming the U5.22 CONFIRMS/producer rule.
